key_insight: Residual learning with convex projection improves quantum error mitigation while ensuring reconstructed density matrices remain physically valid.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports more accurate bound-state simulations on noisy quantum hardware, with performance shaped by training-state selection and regression model choice.
method: Use residual learning to correct noisy quantum-state estimates.
Apply convex projection to enforce physically valid density matrices.
Evaluate Haar-random and VQE-ansatz training states with different regression models.
evidence_signal: IBM hardware tests on three- and four-qubit hypernuclear systems achieved a three-qubit energy of −0.134 MeV versus the ideal −0.135 MeV with 0.999 fidelity, and four-qubit energies of −3.014 and −3.045 MeV with fidelities of 0.995 and 0.998.
watch_item: Evaluation is limited to three- and four-qubit systems; scalability and robustness across training distributions and hardware noise require further validation.
paper_title: Machine Learning-Based Quantum Error Mitigation for Bound-State Simulations
